context:
Start with diagnosis (w1, w4 can run in parallel - they're independent platforms).
For dask-df, focus on the query translator in benchbox/platforms/dataframe/ rather
than test-side workarounds.
For pyspark-df, prefer tightening the availability guard over adding more xfail
complexity to the test.
The reenable-fireducks-after-upstream-fixes TODO is a good structural reference
for this pattern.
description:
Two platform/benchmark combinations were marked xfail in the matrix integration
test (tests/integration/test_local_platform_benchmark_matrix.py) and in e2e tests
to fix a failing test suite (commit 8c0ddcb46, 2026-03-27):

1. dask-df/tpcds - Dask fails on complex TPC-DS expressions (isin and others).
   Related: test_dataframe_platforms.py::TestDaskDataFrameE2E::test_tpch_full_execution
   is also xfail for the same isin issue on TPC-H. Both point to the same root
   cause: Dask's lazy evaluation doesn't support the isin() expression form that
   the BenchBox DataFrame query translator emits.

2. pyspark-df/tpcds - PySpark TPC-DS at SF=1.0 fails in CI without full JVM/Spark
   setup. This is an environment constraint, not a query translation bug. Likely
   fixable by improving the availability check or guard condition rather than
   fixing PySpark itself.

Risk: xfail markers that reference "known runtime failures" without a resolution
path tend to persist indefinitely. This TODO tracks explicit resolution criteria
and required follow-up so each xfail either gets fixed or is consciously accepted
as permanent and documented accordingly.

anti_patterns.dont: add strict=False to the pyspark-df xfail without diagnosing whether the test can even reach the failure
anti_patterns.why: it may already be unreachable via is_dataframe_available

anti_patterns.dont: modify _DATAFRAME_XFAIL_COMBINATIONS to add new entries without creating a corresponding TODO
anti_patterns.why: that is how xfails become permanent

anti_patterns.dont: raise the xfail scope to cover more queries or platforms
